title: Arlington (Dallas metroplex)
prose:
AT&T Stadium sits in Arlington, Texas, a city of roughly 390,000 wedged between Dallas and Fort Worth. Arlington was incorporated in 1884, while the metroplex's anchor city, Dallas, traces its founding to 1841. Together they form the heart of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, one of the largest metropolitan areas in the United States with a population of over 7 million.

Arlington has grown into the metroplex's sports and entertainment hub. Alongside AT&T Stadium, the city is home to the Texas Rangers' Globe Life Field and to Six Flags Over Texas, clustering some of the region's marquee attractions within a single suburban core.

Football culture here belongs less to suburban Arlington than to the wider Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. The region fields MLS side FC Dallas, based in Frisco, and is home to a large and growing Hispanic and Latin American community whose support drives strong followings for Mexican and South American national teams. That appetite for the international game has made AT&T Stadium a natural neutral host: the venue has staged repeat Concacaf Gold Cup matches and 2024 Copa América fixtures, regularly drawing large crowds and cementing the metroplex's place on the continental football map.
